requirement_statement: The application shall not retain personally identifiable user-entered wellbeing records for more than 24 months after the user's last active session.
verbatim_source_text: A digital health application shall retain personally identifiable user-entered wellbeing records for no longer than 24 months after the user's last active session, unless the user has explicitly opted in to longer retention.
condition_trigger: Always, unless the user has explicitly opted in to longer retention
acceptance_criterion: Records identified as personally identifiable wellbeing records are absent from all production stores 24 months after the timestamp of the last active session, absent a recorded opt-in.
verification_method: Inspection of data stores and retention job configuration; records-lifecycle test with clock advance
ambiguity_flags: "Last active session" is not defined in the excerpt; "personally identifiable" is not defined in the excerpt.

requirement_statement: The application shall provide a mechanism by which the user can explicitly opt in to retention longer than 24 months.
verbatim_source_text: ...unless the user has explicitly opted in to longer retention.
condition_trigger: The provider intends to retain records beyond 24 months
acceptance_criterion: An affirmative, user-initiated opt-in control exists; retention beyond 24 months occurs only for users with a recorded opt-in.
verification_method: Inspection of the consent UI and stored consent record
ambiguity_flags: Derived, not stated as a separate requirement. The clause presumes an opt-in mechanism without requiring one. Flag for the paper as an implied capability.

requirement_statement: On a user request to delete their account, the application shall erase all personally identifiable wellbeing records within 30 days.
verbatim_source_text: Where a user requests deletion of their account, the application shall erase all personally identifiable wellbeing records within 30 days of the request.
condition_trigger: A user requests deletion of their account
acceptance_criterion: No personally identifiable wellbeing record for the requesting user is retrievable from any production or backup store more than 30 days after the request timestamp.
verification_method: Deletion test with clock advance; inspection of backup and replica erasure procedure
ambiguity_flags: Silent on backups, replicas and third-party processors; "erase" vs. anonymise is not distinguished.

requirement_statement: Aggregate statistics derived from user records may be retained indefinitely only where they cannot be re-identified.
verbatim_source_text: Aggregate statistics derived from user records may be retained indefinitely provided they cannot be re-identified.
condition_trigger: Aggregate statistics are derived from user records
acceptance_criterion: Any indefinitely retained aggregate passes a documented re-identification risk assessment.
verification_method: Analysis of aggregation method; re-identification risk assessment
verifiability: Judgement-based (no re-identification test or threshold specified)
ambiguity_flags: Permission, not obligation. The binding content is the proviso. No standard or method for establishing non-re-identifiability is named.

requirement_statement: The application shall enable the user to export their complete wellbeing record.
verbatim_source_text: The application shall enable the user to export their complete wellbeing record in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
condition_trigger: Always
acceptance_criterion: An export initiated by the user contains every wellbeing record entry attributable to that user, including free-text entries (per definition 3.4).
verification_method: Export test compared against the stored record set
ambiguity_flags: "Complete" is not scoped against derived or inferred data (e.g. personalisation profiles).

requirement_statement: The export shall be in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
verbatim_source_text: The application shall enable the user to export their complete wellbeing record in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
condition_trigger: Always
acceptance_criterion: The export file parses without OCR or layout inference (e.g. JSON, XML, CSV). A rendered PDF alone fails (see NOTE at 5.2.2).
verification_method: Inspection of export file; machine parse test
verifiability: Partly objective (NOTE 5.2.2 supplies one negative test; ""commonly used"" is not enumerated)
ambiguity_flags: "Commonly used" is undefined; only the PDF counter-example is given.

requirement_statement: All personally identifiable data transmitted between the application and any remote service shall be protected in transit using a current, non-deprecated transport encryption protocol.
verbatim_source_text: All personally identifiable data transmitted between the application and any remote service shall be protected in transit using a current, non-deprecated transport encryption protocol.
condition_trigger: Personally identifiable data is transmitted to any remote service
acceptance_criterion: Every outbound connection carrying personally identifiable data negotiates a transport protocol version not deprecated at the time of assessment; no cleartext fallback path exists.
verification_method: Network traffic capture; TLS configuration scan
verifiability: Objective at a point in time; the ""current
ambiguity_flags: non-deprecated"" baseline moves
column16: No named protocol or version floor; conformance is time-dependent. Covers transit only, not data at rest.

requirement_statement: Where the application collects free-text entries, it shall provide a persistently reachable route to crisis support information from any screen on which free-text entry is possible.
verbatim_source_text: Where an application collects free-text entries from the user, it shall provide the user with a persistently reachable route to crisis support information from any screen on which free-text entry is possible.
condition_trigger: The application collects free-text entries from the user
acceptance_criterion: On every screen offering free-text entry, a control leading to crisis support information is present and reachable without leaving or losing the entry context.
verification_method: Screen-by-screen inspection of all free-text surfaces; navigation test
ambiguity_flags: "Persistently reachable" is not quantified (always visible vs. reachable in N steps). Content and currency of the crisis information are not specified.

requirement_statement: The application shall not present the user with an automated assessment of suicide risk.
verbatim_source_text: The application shall not present the user with an automated assessment of suicide risk.
condition_trigger: Always
acceptance_criterion: No screen, notification or export surfaces a machine-generated suicide risk score, category or equivalent statement to the user.
verification_method: Inspection of all user-facing outputs; review of model outputs surfaced in the UI
verifiability: Objective on presentation; boundary is judgement-based
ambiguity_flags: Prohibits presentation to the user, not internal computation or disclosure to a clinician. Boundary with generic risk-signal messaging is unclear. Prohibitions of this kind need a distinct catalogue treatment from positive obligations.

requirement_statement: The application shall display, on first use, a statement that it is not a substitute for professional care.
verbatim_source_text: The application shall display, on first use, a statement that it is not a substitute for professional care.
condition_trigger: First use of the application
acceptance_criterion: The statement is displayed during the first session, before or at the point of first substantive use.
verification_method: First-run walkthrough on a clean install
ambiguity_flags: "First use" per install, per account or per device is not distinguished; no re-display requirement after updates or reinstall; no acknowledgement requirement.

requirement_statement: Any therapeutic content presented to the user shall carry an identifiable source.
verbatim_source_text: Any therapeutic content presented to the user shall carry an identifiable source and a date of last clinical review.
condition_trigger: Therapeutic content is presented to the user
acceptance_criterion: Each item of therapeutic content displays or links to an attributable source.
verification_method: Content audit against the content inventory
ambiguity_flags: "Therapeutic content" is not defined in the excerpt; the boundary against general psychoeducation or UI copy is open.

requirement_statement: Any therapeutic content presented to the user shall carry a date of last clinical review.
verbatim_source_text: Any therapeutic content presented to the user shall carry an identifiable source and a date of last clinical review.
condition_trigger: Therapeutic content is presented to the user
acceptance_criterion: Each item of therapeutic content displays a date of last clinical review.
verification_method: Content audit against the content inventory
ambiguity_flags: Whether the date must be user-visible or only recorded in metadata is not stated; "clinical review" and reviewer competence are not defined.

requirement_statement: Therapeutic content whose last clinical review is more than 36 months old shall be withdrawn or re-reviewed.
verbatim_source_text: Therapeutic content whose last clinical review is more than 36 months old shall be withdrawn or re-reviewed.
condition_trigger: Last clinical review date is more than 36 months old
acceptance_criterion: No live therapeutic content carries a review date older than 36 months at the time of assessment.
verification_method: Content inventory query against review dates
ambiguity_flags: Disjunctive obligation (withdraw OR re-review): either branch satisfies it, so the catalogue entry must not be split into two requirements.

requirement_statement: The application shall not send engagement-driven notifications between 22:00 and 07:00 in the user's local time zone.
verbatim_source_text: The application shall not send engagement-driven notifications between 22:00 and 07:00 in the user's local time zone unless the user has explicitly configured otherwise.
condition_trigger: Always, unless the user has explicitly configured otherwise
acceptance_criterion: No engagement-driven notification is dispatched within the local 22:00-07:00 window for a user who has not changed the setting; the window follows the device time zone across travel and DST.
verification_method: Notification log review across time zones; scheduled-send test
ambiguity_flags: "Engagement-driven" is not defined and the boundary against essential or safety notifications is open. Classified here as Safety (sleep protection) with Personalisation as secondary.

requirement_statement: The application shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA.
verbatim_source_text: The application shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA.
condition_trigger: Always
acceptance_criterion: All Level A and AA success criteria of WCAG 2.1 are met across the application's screens.
verification_method: WCAG 2.1 AA audit (automated scan plus manual and assistive-technology testing)
verifiability: Objective (external criteria) but high assessment cost
ambiguity_flags: Incorporates ~50 external success criteria by reference: a single catalogue row that expands to a large sub-catalogue. Mobile-app applicability of WCAG is not addressed; no version-drift rule (2.2 / 3.0).

requirement_statement: The application shall permit the user to increase text size to at least 200 % of the default without loss of content or functionality.
verbatim_source_text: The application shall permit the user to increase text size to at least 200 % of the default without loss of content or functionality.
condition_trigger: Always
acceptance_criterion: At 200 % text size, no content is clipped, truncated or overlapped and every control remains operable.
verification_method: Reflow test at 200 % using OS-level and in-app text scaling
ambiguity_flags: Overlaps WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.4 already required by MW-ACC-001: restates a subset explicitly. Note the redundancy in the paper rather than deduplicating, since it signals emphasis. Silent on whether OS-level scaling alone suffices.

requirement_statement: The application shall permit the user to disable all non-essential notifications.
verbatim_source_text: The application shall permit the user to disable all non-essential notifications, and shall retain that preference across application updates.
condition_trigger: Always
acceptance_criterion: An in-app control disables every notification class not classified as essential; after disabling, no non-essential notification is dispatched.
verification_method: Settings inspection; notification dispatch test after opt-out
verifiability: Objective on the control; classification is judgement-based
ambiguity_flags: "Non-essential" is not defined and the essential/non-essential split is left to the provider.

requirement_statement: The application shall retain the user's notification preference across application updates.
verbatim_source_text: The application shall permit the user to disable all non-essential notifications, and shall retain that preference across application updates.
condition_trigger: An application update is installed
acceptance_criterion: The stored preference is unchanged and still enforced after a version upgrade.
verification_method: Upgrade test across at least one major version boundary
ambiguity_flags: Conjunctive clause split into MW-PER-001 and MW-PER-002; each is independently verifiable. Silent on reinstall and on device migration.

requirement_statement: The application shall provide a mechanism by which the user can explicitly configure notification delivery outside the default 22:00-07:00 quiet window.
verbatim_source_text: ...unless the user has explicitly configured otherwise.
condition_trigger: The provider intends to deliver engagement-driven notifications during the quiet window
acceptance_criterion: An explicit, user-initiated setting governs night-time delivery; the default state is quiet-hours enforced.
verification_method: Settings inspection; default-state check on a clean install
ambiguity_flags: Derived, not stated as a separate requirement. Whether "configured otherwise" requires an explicit opt-in or tolerates a pre-set default is not stated.

requirement_statement: Where the application adapts content on the basis of user data, it shall disclose to the user that adaptation is occurring.
verbatim_source_text: Where the application adapts content on the basis of user data, it shall disclose to the user that adaptation is occurring and on what categories of data it is based.
condition_trigger: The application adapts content on the basis of user data
acceptance_criterion: A user-facing disclosure states that content is being adapted.
verification_method: Inspection of the disclosure surface; trace from adaptation features to disclosure text
ambiguity_flags: Conjunctive clause split into MW-PER-004 and MW-PER-005. Timing, placement and prominence of the disclosure are unspecified.

requirement_statement: Where the application adapts content on the basis of user data, it shall disclose on what categories of data the adaptation is based.
verbatim_source_text: Where the application adapts content on the basis of user data, it shall disclose to the user that adaptation is occurring and on what categories of data it is based.
condition_trigger: The application adapts content on the basis of user data
acceptance_criterion: The disclosure enumerates the categories of user data driving adaptation, and the enumeration matches the features actually in use.
verification_method: Disclosure text compared against the data-flow inventory for adaptation features
verifiability: Objective if a data-flow inventory exists
ambiguity_flags: Granularity of "categories" is unspecified. No requirement to allow the user to opt out of, correct or switch off adaptation - a notable gap for this characteristic.
